# README — Tables generated by `Figure_4.R`

This README describes every table exported by `Figure_4.R` (folder `article/tables/Figure_4/`). Figure 4 builds the final signal+seed network for the HPE cohort (case only, no IOP comparison here), enriches each gene with additional variant evidence recovered under relaxed filters, and annotates every gene/edge for prioritization and Cytoscape visualization.

Three levels of variant evidence are used throughout these tables, from strictest to most permissive:

- **`variant` / `seed`** — strict seed variant from the original diagnostic filtering pipeline (`patient_data.R`).
- **`variant_refined`** — variant recovered with relaxed frequency/depth filters (`PRED_value_reworked ≥ 0.7`, pLI ignored) on a gene that is already a cohort-level **signal** gene (network-propagation logic: "this gene already looks important from RWR, does the patient actually carry something in it under looser filters?").
- **`variant_diag`** — variant recovered with more relaxed quality filters (`seq_depth ≥ 10`, `INHOUSE_FREQ ≤ 0.001`, `DB_freq ≤ 0.01`, `PRED_value_reworked ≥ 0.3`) on a gene that is a **known clinical diagnostic gene for that specific patient** (from `clinic_clean.csv`) — clinical logic, independent of the network.
- **`none`** — no variant evidence at any of the above levels.

If a patient qualifies for both `variant_refined` and `variant_diag` on the same variant, `variant_diag` takes priority (direct clinical justification).

---

## 1. `HPE_full_cohort_signal_seed_network_refined.csv`

**What it contains:** the full network of edges among the union of (a) cohort-level signal genes (RWR-propagated, `signal_final = TRUE`, same definition as in Figure 3) and (b) seed genes directly connected to at least one signal gene in the full co-expression network. This is an **edge list**: one row per connection between two genes, with node1 fully annotated on every row.

**Important — duplication:** every edge appears twice, once as `node1 → node2` and once mirrored as `node2 → node1` (`duplicate = FALSE` / `TRUE`), so that every gene has a row where it is `node1` and carries its own full annotation. This is intentional (needed for Cytoscape import) — **filter out `duplicate == TRUE` before any node-level (not edge-level) analysis**, or you will double-count genes.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `node1` | Gene symbol at one end of the edge (the gene whose annotations are on this row). |
| `node2` | Gene symbol at the other end of the edge (its neighbor). |
| `label` | Copy of `node1`, but set to `""` (empty) if `variant_status == "none"` — used directly as the Cytoscape node label, so nodes with zero variant evidence are drawn unlabeled to declutter the network view. |
| `signal` | `TRUE`/`FALSE` — is `node1` a cohort-level signal gene? |
| `seed` | `TRUE`/`FALSE` — is `node1` a seed gene (strict, original filtering) in at least one HPE patient? |
| `seed_n` | Number of HPE patients for whom `node1` is a strict seed gene. |
| `condition` | `node1`'s network status: `"seed+signal"`, `"seed"`, `"signal"` (mutually exclusive labels built from `signal`/`seed`). |
| `degree` | Degree centrality of `node1` in the **full** co-expression network (not just this subnetwork) — same metric as Figures 1 and 3. |
| `cor` | Correlation weight of the specific `node1`–`node2` edge (this is an edge property, not a node property). |
| `link` | Strength category of this specific edge: `"link"` if `cor ≥ 0.4` (strong, regardless of anything else); `"link_weak"` if `cor < 0.4` but this edge is still the strongest connection available to at least one of its two endpoints (i.e. that gene's best option even if weak); `"none"` otherwise. This property is identical on an edge's two mirrored rows. |
| `duplicate` | `FALSE` on the original edge row, `TRUE` on its mirrored counterpart. **Filter to `FALSE` for node-level counts.** |
| `variant_status` | Best (highest-priority) variant evidence available for `node1`: `"variant"` (strict seed) > `"variant_diag"` > `"variant_refined"` > `"none"`. |
| `signal_variant_status` | Combination of `condition` (is `node1` a signal gene or not) and `variant_status`, as an interest-level label: prefixed `signal_` or `non_signal_`, followed by `seed` (variant seed, strict), `variant_diag_excluded` (known diagnostic gene, variant recovered under relaxed filters, but not part of the strict/original seed set — moderate interest, gene already clinically known), `variant_refined` (variant recovered post-RWR on a signal gene — lower interest), or `no_variant` (no variant evidence at all — lowest interest). |
| `HPE_genes` | Literature-based HPE diagnostic tier for `node1`: `"major"` (Dubourg et al., 2018 major causal genes: SHH, ZIC2, SIX3, TGIF1, GLI2, FGF8, FGFR1, DISP1, DLL1), `"minor"` (SHH/Nodal-pathway genes reported in <1% of patients: SUFU, STIL, PTCH1, GAS1, TDGF1, CDON, FOXH1, NODAL, BOC), or `NA` if `node1` is not one of these known HPE genes. |
| `isolated_low_confidence` | `TRUE`/`FALSE` — flags genes with `variant_status` in `{"variant_refined", "none"}` that have **no strong edge** (`link == "link"`) **and no edge at all** (strong or weak) toward a `"seed+signal"` gene. These genes have no credible anchor in the network and were removed before the Cytoscape layout used for the main core network figure (see below). |
| `network_fragment` | Which small, manually-annotated network fragment (`frag1`–`frag13`, or `"isolated"` for 0-neighbor genes) `node1` falls into **after** removing `isolated_low_confidence` nodes from the network, restricted to `link`/`link_weak` edges only. Only populated for genes carrying variant evidence (`variant_status != "none"`); genes with no variant evidence get `NA` regardless of which fragment they physically sit in — same as genes belonging to the main (large) fragment or to `isolated_low_confidence` nodes. See the script comments (section 7ter) for the exact gene lists per fragment. |

**How to read it for node-level questions (e.g. "list every gene and its properties"):** filter to `duplicate == FALSE`, then `distinct(node1, .keep_all = TRUE)` — or simply use table 2 below (`node_recap`), which already does this for you.

**How to read it for edge-level questions (e.g. "who is gene X connected to, and how strongly"):** keep both `duplicate` values, or filter to `node1 == "YOUR_GENE"` to get every edge touching that gene from its own perspective.

---

## 2. `HPE_full_cohort_signal_seed_node_recap_refined.csv`

**What it contains:** the biologist-facing, one-row-per-gene summary table (deduplicated from table 1, `duplicate == FALSE` and one row per distinct `node1`/`gene`), enriched with the count and patient-list of additional variant evidence found under the relaxed filters. This is the primary table to browse gene by gene for prioritization (used, e.g., to build the "signal+seed genes" bibliography tables in the article's Figure 4 section).

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `gene` | Gene symbol (renamed from `node1`). |
| `label` | Same as in table 1 — empty string if `variant_status == "none"`. |
| `condition` | Same as in table 1: `"seed+signal"`, `"seed"`, or `"signal"`. |
| `degree` | Same as in table 1: degree centrality in the full co-expression network. |
| `seed_n` | Same as in table 1: number of HPE patients for whom this gene is a strict seed. |
| `variant_status` | Same as in table 1: best variant evidence level (`variant` > `variant_diag` > `variant_refined` > `none`). |
| `signal_variant_status` | Same as in table 1: combined signal-status × variant-evidence interest label. |
| `HPE_genes` | Same as in table 1: literature HPE tier, `"major"` / `"minor"` / `NA`. |
| `isolated_low_confidence` | Same as in table 1. |
| `network_fragment` | Same as in table 1: `frag1`–`frag13` / `"isolated"` / `NA`. |
| `variant_diag_n_patients` | Number of *additional* HPE patients (beyond the strict seed set) in whom this gene carries a variant recovered via the clinical/diagnostic relaxed-filter route (`variant_diag`). `0` if none. |
| `variant_diag_patients` | Semicolon-separated list of the patient IDs contributing that `variant_diag` evidence. `NA` if none. |
| `variant_refined_n_patients` | Number of *additional* HPE patients in whom this gene carries a variant recovered via the network/signal-gene relaxed-filter route (`variant_refined`). `0` if none. |
| `variant_refined_patients` | Semicolon-separated list of the patient IDs contributing that `variant_refined` evidence. `NA` if none. |

**How to read it:** the table is pre-sorted by (1) strict-seed status first (`variant_status == "variant"` genes on top), then (2) `seed_n` descending, then (3) `degree` descending — so the most patient-supported, most-connected known seed genes appear first. Use `variant_diag_n_patients`/`variant_refined_n_patients` > 0 to identify genes whose case is strengthened by evidence beyond the original strict seed calling, and check the corresponding `_patients` column to see exactly which individuals contribute that extra evidence (useful for going back to the raw VCF/clinical record if needed).

**Note on `network_fragment` and Figure 4 parts A/B in the article:** part A of the article's Figure 4 section covers the "main core" network — every seed+signal gene *not* assigned to a small fragment (i.e. `network_fragment` is `NA` and the gene is not `isolated_low_confidence`). Part B covers the genes with a non-`NA` `network_fragment` value (the twelve seed+signal genes distributed across eight small peripheral fragments, as discussed in the article draft).
